questions.text:
An electrical installation consists of a DC motor driving a water pump. The motor operates on a $250$ V DC supply and draws a steady current of $20$ A. The internal armature resistance of the motor is $0.55\ \Omega$. The pump draws water from a large underground tank and discharges it to the atmosphere at a height of $5$ m above the tank's water level. The discharge pipe has a uniform cross-sectional area of $25\ \mathrm{cm^2}$, and the steady volumetric flow rate of the water is $10$ L/s.

Assume that all mechanical energy losses in the pump manifest entirely as fluid friction. If the ratio of the electrical power dissipated as heat in the motor's armature to the mechanical power dissipated as heat due to fluid friction in the pump is $\dfrac{11}{N}$, find the value of the integer $N$.
(Take the density of water as $1000\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}$ and $g=10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$)

questions.text:
An antique artifact, modeled as a perfect solid cylinder of radius $1$ cm and height $4$ cm, is to be restored by completely submerging it as a cathode in an electroplating bath. The electrolytic bath contains an aqueous solution of $AuCl_3$ and $CuSO_4$.

A constant current of $9.65$ A is passed through the cell for exactly $15$ minutes. During this time, a Gold-Copper alloy is deposited uniformly over the entire surface area of the artifact. It is observed that the deposited alloy contains gold and copper in a $1:3$ molar ratio.

Assume the current efficiency for the deposition of the alloy is $100\%$ (no side reactions occur), the volume of the alloy is the sum of the volumes of the individual deposited metals, and the thickness of the plating is negligible compared to the dimensions of the cylinder for area calculations.

Given: Molar mass of Au $=197$ g/mol, Cu $=63.5$ g/mol; Density of solid Au $=19.7\ \mathrm{g/cm^3}$, Cu $=6.35\ \mathrm{g/cm^3}$; $F=96500$ C/mol.
What is the thickness of the deposited alloy layer?

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
For bimolecular gas-phase reactions, the classical Arrhenius equation is often refined using the kinetic collision theory: $k=A'T^{1/2}e^{-E_0/RT}$, where $E_0$ is the threshold energy of the reaction and $A'$ is a temperature-independent constant.

Consider two simultaneous, parallel bimolecular gas-phase elementary reactions between $A$ and $B$: Pathway 1: $A+B\xrightarrow{k_1}Y$; Pathway 2: $A+B\xrightarrow{k_2}Z$. The threshold energies are $E_{0,1}=20$ kcal/mol and $E_{0,2}=23$ kcal/mol. Both pathways strictly follow the collision theory model.

At a constant temperature of $500$ K, the rate of formation of product $Y$ is exactly twice the rate of formation of product $Z$. The observed effective activation energy for the overall disappearance of the reactants is defined by $E_{a,eff}=RT^2\dfrac{d(\ln k_{eff})}{dT}$, where $k_{eff}$ is the effective overall rate constant.

If the effective activation energy for the overall reaction at $500$ K is $E$ kcal/mol, determine the value of $10E$. (Given: $R=2\ \mathrm{cal\,K^{-1}mol^{-1}}$)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Ice that burns! Methane hydrate: under high-pressure and low-temperature conditions, methane forms methane hydrate, consisting of single molecules of natural gas trapped within crystalline cavities formed by frozen water molecules. The main characteristic of the structure is dodecahedra formed from $20$ water molecules. The unit cell can be thought of as a body-centred cubic arrangement built from these dodecahedra, which are almost spherical objects. The dodecahedra are connected via additional water molecules located on the faces of the unit cell. Two water molecules can be found within each face of the unit cell. The unit cell has an edge dimension of $1.182$ nm. There are two types of cavities: one is the internal space ($X$) in the dodecahedra, somewhat smaller than the other type of voids ($Y$), of which there are $6$ per unit cell.
How many water molecules are there in a unit cell of the crystal?
